n2687d8c27e8.s: Which Governor-General followed Cornwallis's second term in 1805?
n2687d8c27e8.x: Cornwallis's second term (1805) was followed by Sir George Barlow and then by Minto I; Wellesley served before it.

nindian-history-25-18.s: In which year did the Archaeological Survey become a separate department?
nindian-history-25-18.x: The Archaeological Survey became a separate department in 1871; Marshall took charge in 1902 and the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act came in 1904.

nda842c3edfb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Act of 1786?
o: It let the Governor-General override his Council in special cases
It remedied the repeated outvoting of the Governor-General by his Council
It was passed to meet Lord Cornwallis's condition for accepting office
It remedied the absence of a Board of Control
nda842c3edfb.x: The Act of 1786 fixed the outvoting of the Governor-General by giving him an override power; the Board of Control had already been created by Pitt's India Act, 1784.

new.s: Who was the first Governor of Bengal (1758)?
new.x: Robert Clive became the first Governor of Bengal in 1758; Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773).

new.s: The office of Viceroy and Governor-General was created by the:
new.x: The Government of India Act, 1858 created the title Viceroy, first held by Lord Canning; the Charter Act of 1833 created the Governor-General of India.

new.s: Who was the last Governor-General of Bengal?
new.x: William Bentinck was the last Governor-General of Bengal and became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833.

new.s: Which Governor-General immediately preceded Marquess Hastings (1813-23)?
new.x: Minto I served 1807-13 and was followed by Marquess Hastings; the Charter Act of 1813 fell in this change-over.

new.s: William Bentinck's tenure as Governor-General was:
new.x: Bentinck served 1828-35; 1833-35 is only his time as Governor-General of India, and 1823-28 was Amherst's tenure.

new.s: Who served as Governor-General between William Bentinck and Auckland?
new.x: Sir Charles Metcalfe (1835-36) came between Bentinck (1828-35) and Auckland (1836-42).

new.s: The Code of Gentoo Laws (1776) was prepared during the tenure of:
new.x: The Code of Gentoo Laws, Halhed's translation of the Vivadarnavasetu, came in 1776 under Warren Hastings.

new.s: The Public Works Department was set up in 1854 by:
new.x: Dalhousie set up the Public Works Department in 1854, along with railway, post and telegraph development.

new.s: The Treaty of Amritsar (1809) with Ranjit Singh was concluded by:
new.x: Minto I concluded the Treaty of Amritsar in 1809; Bentinck's treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh came in 1831.

new.s: The Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act of 1845 was passed under:
new.x: The Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act came in 1845 under Hardinge I; Ellenborough is linked with the abolition of slavery (1843).

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Hardinge I – Caste Disabilities Removal Act
new.x: The Caste Disabilities Removal Act (1850) was passed under Dalhousie, not Hardinge I.

new.s: The Mahalwari system (1822), associated with Holt Mackenzie, was introduced under:
new.x: Mahalwari was introduced in 1822 under Marquess Hastings; Bentinck later revised it by Regulation IX of 1833.

new.s: The Subsidiary Alliance (1798) was introduced by:
new.x: Wellesley introduced the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.

new.s: The Widow Remarriage Act was passed in 1856 under:
new.x: The Widow Remarriage Act of 1856 belongs to Dalhousie's tenure (1848-56).

new.s: The policy of non-intervention is associated with:
new.x: Sir John Shore followed non-intervention; Marquess Hastings followed a policy of intervention and wars.

new.s: Which Governor-General extended irrigation and started famine relief?
new.x: Auckland extended irrigation and started famine relief; Ellenborough ended the Afghan War.

new.s: Warren Hastings stopped the annual tribute paid to Shah Alam of:
new.x: Warren Hastings stopped the Rs 26 lakh tribute to Shah Alam.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Dalhousie:
1. He applied the Doctrine of Lapse.
2. He ended the Afghan War.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Dalhousie is linked with the Doctrine of Lapse; the Afghan War was ended by Ellenborough.

new.s: Which Governor-General showed a preference for English education?
new.x: Hardinge I is noted for his preference for English education.

new.s: The Anglo-Nepal War (1814-16) and the Treaty of Sugauli belong to the tenure of:
new.x: Marquess Hastings fought the Anglo-Nepal War (1814-16), ended by the Treaty of Sugauli.

new.s: The First Anglo-Burmese War (1824) took place under:
new.x: Amherst fought the First Anglo-Burmese War (1824), ended by the Treaty of Yandabo (1826); the Second Burmese War was under Dalhousie.

new.s: The First Anglo-Afghan War (1838) began during the tenure of:
new.x: The First Anglo-Afghan War began in 1838 under Auckland; Ellenborough later ended the Afghan War.

new.s: The Treaty of Lahore (1846) was signed during the tenure of:
new.x: The Treaty of Lahore (1846), after the First Anglo-Sikh War, belongs to Hardinge I, not Ellenborough.

new.s: The Treaty of Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War during the tenure of:
new.x: The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of Salbai (1782) under Warren Hastings.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The First Anglo-Sikh War was under Hardinge I; Ellenborough is linked with the annexation of Sindh (1843).

new.s: Under Wellesley, the Ceded Districts came to the Company in:
new.x: The Nizam's alliance came in 1798, the Ceded Districts in 1800, and Andhra was merged into Madras in 1801.

new.s: Warren Hastings was impeached in the British Parliament in:
new.x: Hastings was impeached in 1787; the trial ran from 1788 to 1795.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the impeachment of Warren Hastings:
1. It was led by Edmund Burke.
2. The judicial murder of Nand Kumar was one of the charges.
3. The trial ended in his conviction in 1795.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Burke and the Whigs led the impeachment and Nand Kumar's judicial murder was a charge; the trial ended in acquittal in 1795.

new.s: Who described himself as the 'Bengal Tiger'?
new.x: Richard Colley Wellesley called himself the 'Bengal Tiger'; Clive was the 'heaven-born general'.

new.s: Who is known as the 'Father of Civil Services in India'?
new.x: Cornwallis reformed the services and created the Covenanted Civil Service; Warren Hastings only laid the foundation.

new.s: Who is called the 'heaven-born general' and the founder of British power in India?
new.x: Robert Clive is called the founder of British power in India and the 'heaven-born general'.

new.s: The real name of Marquess Hastings was:
new.x: Marquess Hastings was Francis Rawdon-Hastings, also called Lord Moira.

new.s: Who is called the 'Father of Modern Western Education in India'?
new.x: William Bentinck is called the Father of Modern Western Education in India.

new.s: The 'Blue Water Policy' is associated with:
new.x: Francisco de Almeida followed the Blue Water Policy; Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510.

new.s: Who was the first Indian journalist to be jailed (1883)?
new.x: Surendranath Banerjee was jailed on 2 April 1883 for an article in The Bengalee.

new.s: In which year did Mayo's Resolution begin financial decentralisation?
new.x: Mayo's Resolution of 14 December 1870 began financial decentralisation.

new.s: Who divided revenue heads into imperial, provincial and divided heads in 1882?
new.x: Ripon (1882) divided revenue heads into imperial, provincial and divided; Lytton had widened the provincial heads in 1877.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about financial decentralisation:
1. Under Mayo, provinces got fixed annual grants for police, jails, education, medical services and roads.
2. Provinces could raise local taxes to balance their budgets.
3. Lytton widened the provincial heads in 1877.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: Mayo gave fixed grants and power to raise local taxes, and Lytton widened the provincial heads in 1877.

new.s: Lord Mayo was assassinated in the Andamans in 1872 by:
new.x: Mayo was killed by the convict Sher Ali Afridi in the Andamans in 1872; Rash Behari Bose and Sachin Sanyal threw a bomb at Hardinge II.

new.s: Who was the first and last Indian Governor-General?
new.x: C. Rajagopalachari (1948-50) was the first and last Indian Governor-General.

new.s: How many Viceroys ruled India from 1858 to 1947?
new.x: 21 Viceroys ruled India from 1858 to 1947.

new.s: The Wahabi movement is associated with the viceroyalty of:
new.x: Elgin I (1862-63) faced the Wahabi movement; Elgin II faced famine and plague in 1896-97.

new.s: Which Viceroy abolished income tax?
new.x: Northbrook (1872-76) abolished income tax; Canning had introduced it.

new.s: Lytton reduced the maximum age for the ICS examination from 21 to:
new.x: Lytton cut the ICS age from 21 to 19.

new.s: The Arms Act of 1878 was passed during the viceroyalty of:
new.x: Lytton passed the Arms Act and the Vernacular Press Act in 1878.

new.s: Rajkot College and the Department of Agriculture and Commerce are associated with:
new.x: Mayo founded Mayo College (Ajmer) and Rajkot College and set up the Department of Agriculture and Commerce.

new.s: Rand and Ayerst were killed by the Chapekar brothers (1897) during the viceroyalty of:
new.x: The killing of Rand and Ayerst in 1897 happened under Elgin II, during the famine and plague of 1896-97.

new.s: The Second Factory Act (1891) was passed under:
new.x: Lansdowne passed the Second Factory Act (1891); the first Factory Act (1881) was under Ripon.

new.s: The Durand Commission (1893) on the Afghan boundary was appointed under:
new.x: The Durand Commission of 1893 belongs to Lansdowne's viceroyalty.

new.s: The memoir 'My Indian Years' was written by:
new.x: Hardinge II wrote 'My Indian Years'; Wavell's memoir is 'The Viceroy's Journal'.

new.s: 'The Viceroy's Journal' is the memoir of:
new.x: 'The Viceroy's Journal' is Wavell's memoir.

new.s: The Communal Award and the Poona Pact belong to the viceroyalty of:
new.x: Willingdon (1931-36) saw the Communal Award and the Poona Pact; Irwin saw the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

new.s: Separate electorates were introduced by the Indian Councils Act, 1909 during the viceroyalty of:
new.x: The Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909) under Minto II introduced separate electorates.

new.s: The Royal Commission on Labour (1929) was appointed during the viceroyalty of:
new.x: The Royal Commission on Labour (1929) belongs to Irwin's viceroyalty.

new.s: The Wavell Plan and the Simla Conference failed in:
new.x: The Wavell Plan and Simla Conference (1945) failed on Jinnah's stand.

new.s: Mountbatten replaced Wavell after Attlee's statement of:
new.x: Attlee's statement of 20 February 1947 led to Mountbatten replacing Wavell; 18 July 1947 is the date of the Indian Independence Act.

new.s: The Delhi Durbar of 1911 marked the coronation of:
new.x: The 1911 Durbar marked the coronation of George V and Queen Mary; the 1903 Durbar was for Edward VII.

new.s: The Delhi Durbar of 1903, for the coronation of Edward VII, was held under:
new.x: Curzon held the 1903 Durbar for Edward VII; Lytton held the 1877 Durbar and Hardinge II the 1911 Durbar.

new.s: The Partition of Bengal came into effect on:
new.x: The Partition was announced on 20 July 1905 and took effect on 16 October 1905; it was annulled on 12 December 1911.

new.s: Which was the only Delhi Durbar attended by the monarch?
new.x: The 1911 Durbar, for George V and Queen Mary, was the only one attended by the monarch.

new.s: John Marshall took charge as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey in:
new.x: Curzon appointed John Marshall, who took charge in 1902.

new.s: The AMASR Act, 1958 protects monuments older than:
new.x: The AMASR Act 1958 protects monuments over 100 years old.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the three Indians nominated under the Indian Councils Act, 1861?
new.x: The three Indians nominated in 1861 were the Raja of Benaras, the Maharaja of Patiala and Sir Dinkar Rao.

new.s: The First Factory Act (1881) banned employment of children below the age of:
new.x: The First Factory Act of 1881 under Ripon banned the employment of children below 7.

new.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1861, an Ordinance issued by the Governor-General could last at most:
new.x: The 1861 Act let the Governor-General issue Ordinances lasting up to six months.

new.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Ilbert Bill
2. Royal Titles Act
3. Indian Councils Act (Lansdowne)
4. Vernacular Press Act
new.x: Royal Titles Act (1876), Vernacular Press Act (1878), Ilbert Bill (1883), Indian Councils Act (1892).

new.s: The Indian Universities Act of 1904 was passed during the viceroyalty of:
new.x: Curzon passed the Indian Universities Act in 1904, not Lansdowne; the first universities came in 1857 under Canning.

new.s: The Strachey Famine Commission (1880) was appointed by:
new.x: Lytton appointed the Strachey Famine Commission; Lyall was under Elgin II and MacDonnell under Curzon.

new.s: The Scott-Moncrieff Commission (1901) dealt with:
new.x: The Scott-Moncrieff Commission (1901) under Curzon dealt with irrigation; the Frazer Commission dealt with police.

new.s: In 1767 Parliament capped the Company's dividend at:
new.x: In 1767 Parliament capped the dividend at 10 per cent and made the Company pay £400,000 a year.

new.s: In 1767 the Company was made to pay the state, every year, for its territorial revenues:
new.x: The 1767 terms required the Company to pay £400,000 a year to the state.

new.s: Besides the Select Committee, which body did Parliament appoint in 1772 to inquire into Company affairs?
new.x: In 1772 Parliament appointed a Select Committee (Burgoyne) and a Secret Committee; their reports led to the Regulating Act.

new.s: Under the Regulating Act, 1773, the Governor-General's council had how many members?
new.x: The Act gave the Governor-General a council of four: Philip Francis, Clavering, Monson and Barwell.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Governor-General's council named in the Regulating Act?
new.x: Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court; the council was Francis, Clavering, Monson and Barwell.

new.s: Who was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta?
new.x: Sir Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774).

new.s: Under the Regulating Act, 1773, the presidencies of Bombay and Madras were:
o: placed under the Board of Control
new.x: The Act made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General with supervisory powers and subordinated Bombay and Madras to Bengal.

new.s: The Council–Court clashes caused by the Supreme Court's undefined jurisdiction were remedied by the:
new.x: The 1781 Act of Settlement exempted official acts and revenue from the Supreme Court's jurisdiction.

new.s: Warren Hastings was repeatedly outvoted under the Regulating Act because the Governor-General had:
new.x: Decisions were by majority and the Governor-General had only a casting vote, so Francis, Clavering and Monson could outvote him.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Amending Act, 1781:
1. It exempted the Governor-General and Council from the Supreme Court for acts in their official capacity.
2. It excluded revenue matters from the Court's jurisdiction.
3. It created the Board of Control.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 1781 Act exempted official acts and excluded revenue matters; the Board of Control came with Pitt's India Act, 1784.

new.s: The Amending Act of 1781 is also known as the:
new.x: The Amending Act of 1781 is called the Act of Settlement; it curbed the Supreme Court.

new.s: The Board of Control was created by the:
new.x: Pitt's India Act, 1784 created the Board of Control, not the Regulating Act of 1773.

new.s: The Board of Control under Pitt's India Act had up to how many commissioners?
new.x: The Board of Control had up to six commissioners, including a Secretary of State and the Chancellor of the Exchequer.

new.s: Under the dual system of Pitt's India Act, the Company's commercial affairs remained with the:
new.x: Commercial affairs stayed with the Court of Directors while political affairs went to the Board of Control.

new.s: Besides the power to override his council, the Act of 1786 made the Governor-General the:
o: President of the Board of Control
new.x: The Act of 1786 let the Governor-General override his council and also be Commander-in-Chief.

new.s: The Charter Act of 1793 extended the overriding power to the:
new.x: The Charter Act of 1793 extended the overriding power to the governors of the presidencies.

new.s: Which Act came between the Regulating Act (1773) and Pitt's India Act (1784)?
new.x: The order is Regulating Act 1773, Amending Act 1781, Pitt's India Act 1784, Act of 1786.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Pitt's India Act (1784) set up the dual system; the Board of Control is 1784, the override power 1786 and the Act of Settlement 1781.

new.s: The Supreme Court at Madras, serving British subjects in the Madras Presidency including Andhra, was set up in:
new.x: The Madras Supreme Court was set up in 1801; the Calcutta Supreme Court dates from 1774.
